The Betrayal of Judas

Scriptural scenes

The Betrayal of Judas

Judas receives the thirty pieces of silver

What is depictedHistory and traditionPublished explanationSources

Scripture

Matthew 26:14–16

Matthew 26:47–50

King James Version · Scripture previews

The betrayal of Judas includes the agreement to hand over Christ and the later arrest. The historical icon displayed here specifically depicts the payment of the thirty pieces of silver, rather than the kiss in the garden.

[1] Matthew 26:14–16 and 47–50; distinct episodes in the betrayal

What is depicted

The catalogue identifies Judas Iscariot receiving the thirty pieces of silver. It attributes the icon to an Old Believers’ workshop in Moscow or Yaroslavl at the end of the nineteenth century. Its specific scene is the agreement and payment, so it is not captioned as the garden arrest.

[2] Exact artwork file: Description, Creator, Date, Credit and licence fields; complete downloaded image visually compared

History and tradition

Then one of the twelve, called Judas Iscariot, went unto the chief priests,

And said unto them, What will ye give me, and I will deliver him unto you? And they covenanted with him for thirty pieces of silver.

And from that time he sought opportunity to betray him.

[1] Matthew 26:14–16

The OCA’s Holy Thursday account places Judas’s betrayal beside the supper, describing his departure from the light of the Upper Room. Its explanation concerns the rejection of communion and love; the narrative icon provides a different moment within the same Gospel sequence.

[3] Holy Thursday account, discussion of Judas and the betrayal

Published explanation

And while he yet spake, lo, Judas, one of the twelve, came, and with him a great multitude with swords and staves, from the chief priests and elders of the people.

Now he that betrayed him gave them a sign, saying, Whomsoever I shall kiss, that same is he: hold him fast.

And forthwith he came to Jesus, and said, Hail, master; and kissed him.

And Jesus said unto him, Friend, wherefore art thou come? Then came they, and laid hands on Jesus, and took him.

[1] Matthew 26:47–50
